title.narrative: Lifesaving humanitarian FSA (Envelope 1) and WASH (Envelope 2) assistance for vulnerable IDPs, returnees and host communities in Qatana subdistrict in Rural Damascus

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed project aims to improve the living situation of vulnerable populations in Qatana, including returnees, IDPs and the host community, by providing lifesaving agricultural and livelihood support and increasing equitable access to safe water and sanitation services. The community of Qatana is experiencing severe water scarcity, impacting the sustainability of their farmlands and ability to meet their basic needs. Through a multi-sectoral approach that focuses on rehabilitation of WASH infrastructural facilities, agricultural inputs distribution and capacity strengthening, ZOA aims to provide sustained access to essential services to IDPs, returnees and host communities, while promoting sustainable livelihoods and improving community resilience.lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtDuring the conflict’s peak, a quarter of the population in Qatana fled the subdistrict. In the same period, the community in Qatana absorbed large numbers of displaced people from neighboring conflict areas. Qatana also experienced an influx of returnees following the recent political changes, including families returning from Lebanon to their place of origin. UNHCR data mentions 1,184 returnee HHs, (4,908 individuals) between 8 of December 2024 and 26 June 2025. ZOA's needs assessment in Qatana revealed well-established social cohesion and interaction among the different groups, as well as their shared need for WASH and livelihood assistance.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtSince the onset of the crisis in Syria, the community in Qatana has endured a significant disruption in stabilizing their sources of income. Before the crisis, the community relied on agriculture as its main source of income. However, many farmers have turned to other sources of income due to the acute challenges they face in securing income from agriculture. Agricultural practices are disturbed due to constrained access to land due to past insecurity, crippling water scarcity from drought and rising input costs. At the same time, the community in Qatana face an increasing need for reliable and sustainable access to water for drinking. The main water wells feeding the water network in Qatana need rehabilitation and the installation of a solar system to sustain sufficient water supply. The ongoing crisis also neglected the maintenance of Qatana’s sewage network, showing deterioration and leaks, which is increasing public health risks. lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtBased on these needs (please also see full needs assessment report uploaded) and in line of the call sectoral eligible interventions as well as location the proposal includes the following activities in Qatana community:lt/pgtltpgtltspangt1. Food Security and Agriculture (FSA):lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtltbrgtlt/spangtlt/pgtltulgtltligtRltspangtapid distribution of agricultural inputs (seeds, fertilizers, pesticides, equipment) for seasonal crops for 700 farmers, combined with urgent training for farmers (training on water conservation).lt/spangtlt/ligtltligtltspangtlt/spangtLivestock emergency support: Distribution of inputs for livestock (fodder, inputs for apiculture) for 300 farmers.lt/ligtlt/ulgtltdivgtltpgt2. WASH:lt/pgtltulgtltligtRehabilitation of the sewage network serving 5,000 people in Qatana community, combined with operations and maintenance training.lt/ligtltligtRehabilitation and solarization of the “Water Unit Well” serving 15,000 people, combined with operations and maintenance training.lt/ligtlt/ulgtlt/divgtltpgtWith this response, the proposed project is in line with the allocation priorities of addressing critical food security gaps and promoting lifesaving agricultural and livelihood support (Priority 1.8, Envelope 1) and ensuring equitable access to safe water and sanitation services for returnees and communities of origin and reducing public health risks during reintegration (Priority 2.9, Envelope 2).ltbrgtlt/pgt
